newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN alarmed by spreading typhoid fever in Tajikistan.
newsitem.headline: UN alarmed by spreading typhoid fever in Tajikistan.

text.p: The World Health Organisation expressed alarm on Friday over a spreading typhoid fever outbreak in Tajikistan and said it feared the number of cases could soar from the current 5,000 to 60,000.

Since January, typhoid fever has claimed 46 lives in the Central Asian country, which had a similar outbreak last year when overflow from old sewage systems following heavy rains contaminated the drinking water, the U.N. agency said.
The source of the outbreak was unclear but water in the capital Dushanbe has not been treated for months because a lack of resources forced the local chlorine factory to shut down.

A WHO statement said the government had appealed to the agency to help stop the epidemic, but security precautions taken by U.N. staff in the country following a recent series of kidnappings by armed rebels meant the international response would be limited.
Part of the emergency relief and medical supplies would be financed with a new $1 million grant from Japan, WHO said.
The mountainous former Soviet republic, one of the world's poorest, has been torn apart by four years of tribal conflict between the pro-Islamic opposition and the former communists in power.
